transcript.text: I can certainly help with that. The most common reason a washing machine won't spin is that it hasn't drained the water first; the machine has a safety feature that prevents spinning if there is still water in the drum. This is often caused by a blockage in the pump filter or drain hose. Please check the pump filter (usually behind a small flap at the bottom front) for any debris like coins, hair, or lint. Also, let me know: when you start a cycle, does it attempt to drain but fail, or does it just stop without draining?
it drains ok, no water left in the drum. just the one thing came out soaking wet, the spin sounded like it tried then gave up

Since it drains fine but the sound suggests it tried to engage and then stopped, this often happens for two reasons: either a single heavy item (like a towel or jeans) has clumped on one side and triggered an 'unbalanced load' safety stop, or there is a minor motor issue like worn carbon brushes. To tell them apart, please run a 'Spin Only' cycle with the drum empty. If it spins up properly when empty, the problem was just the load distribution (you can fix this by spreading clothes out evenly next time). If it still makes that struggling noise and won't spin even when empty, we will need to look at the motor or belt.
ok i ran a rinse and spin with the mat plus a couple of towels and it spun up fine, mat came out damp not dripping. what does that mean?

That means the machine is working perfectly and your issue was simply an unbalanced load. Washing machines have a safety feature that stops them from spinning if they detect the weight is all on one side—this often happens with heavy items like bath mats or towels clumping together. Since it spun up fine when you added more items to balance the weight, there is no mechanical fault. To avoid this in future, try not to wash single heavy items alone; adding a few smaller towels helps distribute the weight evenly around the drum.
